title: 5 V 信号进 3.3 V 引脚：分压，或者用耐 5 V 的引脚
summary: 一个按键模拟 5 V 传感器的输出。起始电路把 5 V 直接接到了不耐 5 V 的 PA0。拆掉它，改用分压接 PA0，再直接接一个耐 5 V 的 FT 引脚。
concepts: 分压电平转换 divider level shifting
保护二极管 / 钳位电流 clamp diode current
description: 按键把开发板的 5V 脚接到信号线 SIG5（10 kΩ 下拉到 GND），按下就是“传感器输出高”。两种接法：(a) SIG5 → 10 kΩ → PA0 → 20 kΩ → GND，PA0 是不耐 5 V 的 ADC 引脚；(b) SIG5 直接接耐 5 V 的 FT 引脚（参考答案 PB12）。起始电路里 SIG5 直接接在 PA0 上。

cards.title: 5 V 直接进 PA0
text: 起始电路里，一个**按键**在扮演“5 V 传感器”：按下时，它把开发板的 **5V** 脚接到信号线上。按键现在是按下的。
信号线**直接**插在 **PA0** 上。PA0 是一个普通的 3.3 V 引脚。
看右边的**「诊断」**：PA0 怎么了？电流是从哪条路跑走的？

cards.title: 引脚里藏着一只二极管
text: - 普通引脚里面有一只**保护二极管**，从引脚通向 3V3。引脚电压一比 3V3 高出一个二极管压降，它就导通——就是 5.1 里那只单向阀。
![](fig:clamp)
- 5 V 和 3V3 之间只隔着这只二极管，电流大得吓人。引脚会烧坏，3V3 电源也被“倒灌”抬高。
- 办法一：**分压**。两个电阻把 5 V 缩成三分之二：
![](fig:divider)
- 代入整 5 V：$5 × \frac{20}{10 + 20} ≈ 3.33$ V，正好落在 3.3 V 附近。开发板的 5V 脚其实还要低一点，所以更安全。
- 办法二：Blue Pill 的 **FT 引脚**（5.2 的 Blue Pill 课讲过）。它们里面**没有**通往 3V3 的那只二极管，5 V 信号可以直接接。

cards.title: 两条安全的路
text: - 先**拆掉** SIG5 到 PA0 的那根线。
- **直接接**：SIG5 再用一根线接到一个 **FT 引脚**（下排，例如 **PB12**）。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**。通过后按住按键，量两个引脚的电压，再算分压比。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **5 V 不能直接碰不耐 5 V 的引脚**：引脚里的保护二极管会把它接到 3V3 上。
- 分压只适合**单向、慢速**的信号。几十 kΩ 的电阻和引脚电容会让边沿变缓；快信号用电平转换芯片。
- FT 引脚有两个例外：当 **ADC** 用时不耐 5 V；接 5 V 信号时**不要打开内部上拉**，否则电流会从上拉电阻倒灌进 3V3。
- 真实项目里的坑：**ESP32 没有任何耐 5 V 的引脚**，5 V 传感器（比如超声波模块的回波脚）一定要分压。

caption.text: 5V 直接接到 PA0：引脚里的保护二极管 D 导通，电流 I_D 从 5 V 灌进 3V3。

i18n.en: 5V wired straight to PA0: the pin's protection diode D conducts, and I_D pours from 5 V into 3V3.

caption.text: R1 和 R2 把 SIG5 缩成三分之二再送给 PA0：电压不再高过 3V3，二极管不导通。

i18n.en: R1 and R2 shrink SIG5 to two thirds before it reaches PA0: the voltage no longer rises above 3V3, and the diode stays off.

en.title: A 5 V signal into a 3.3 V pin: divide it, or use a 5 V-tolerant pin
en.summary: A pushbutton plays a 5 V sensor's output. The starting circuit wires 5 V straight into PA0, which is not 5 V-tolerant. Remove that, feed PA0 through a divider, and wire a 5 V-tolerant FT pin directly.
en.description: The button connects the board's 5V pin to the signal line SIG5 (10 kΩ pull-down to GND): pressed = "sensor output HIGH". Two ways in: (a) SIG5 → 10 kΩ → PA0 → 20 kΩ → GND, PA0 being an ADC pin that is not 5 V-tolerant; (b) SIG5 straight to a 5 V-tolerant FT pin (PB12 in the reference). In the starting circuit SIG5 goes straight to PA0.

cards.title: 5 V straight into PA0
text: In the starting circuit a **pushbutton** plays a "5 V sensor": pressed, it connects the board's **5V** pin to the signal line. The button is pressed right now.
The signal line goes **straight** into **PA0**, an ordinary 3.3 V pin.
Look at the **diagnostics** on the right: what happened to PA0? Which way is the current escaping?

cards.title: A diode hidden inside the pin
text: - An ordinary pin has a **protection diode** inside, from the pin to 3V3. As soon as the pin is one diode drop above 3V3, it conducts — the one-way valve from 5.1.
![](fig:clamp)
- Only that diode sits between 5 V and 3V3, so the current is frightening. The pin is destroyed, and the 3V3 supply is pushed up from behind.
- Fix one: a **divider**. Two resistors shrink 5 V to two thirds:
![](fig:divider)
- With a round 5 V: $5 × \frac{20}{10 + 20} ≈ 3.33$ V, right around 3.3 V. The board's 5V pin is actually a little lower, which makes it safer still.
- Fix two: the Blue Pill's **FT pins** (from the Blue Pill lesson in 5.2). They have **no** diode to 3V3 inside, so a 5 V signal can go straight in.

cards.title: Two safe paths
text: - First **remove** the wire from SIG5 to PA0.
- **Divider**: SIG5 → **`10 kΩ`** → PA0's column → **`20 kΩ`** → GND.
- **Direct**: one more wire from SIG5 to an **FT pin** (bottom row, for example **PB12**).
- Press **Check my circuit**. Once it passes, hold the button down, measure both pins' voltages, and work out the divider ratio.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **5 V must never touch a pin that is not 5 V-tolerant**: the pin's protection diode connects it to 3V3.
- A divider only suits **one-way, slow** signals. Tens of kΩ together with the pin's capacitance slow the edges down; fast signals need a level-shifter chip.
- FT pins have two exceptions: used as an **ADC** input they are not 5 V-tolerant, and with a 5 V signal on them **don't turn on the internal pull-up**, or current flows back through it into 3V3.
- A real-world catch: **the ESP32 has no 5 V-tolerant pins at all**, so a 5 V sensor (an ultrasonic module's echo pin, say) always needs a divider.

compare: - Divider: V(SIG3) = 4.69 × 20k/(10k + 20k) = **3.13 V**, above VIH, so it reads 1; the ADC reads **3879** (3.13 V).
- FT pin: PB12 = **4.69 V**, reads 1, and no current flows into the pin.
- Released: the pull-down takes both paths to 0 V and they read 0.

- Starting board: 5 V straight into PA0 forward-biases the pin's internal **clamp diode** to 3V3. With almost no source resistance the diode carries **52 mA** (the STM32 allows only about 5 mA of injected current), and that current back-powers the whole 3V3 rail.
**Why an FT pin copes**: an FT pin has **no** clamp diode to VDD (it uses a different protection structure), so its input may go to VDD + 4 V (5.5 V max in the datasheet). Two exceptions:
- **Not 5 V tolerant in analog (ADC) mode** — used as an ADC input, an FT pin is damaged by 5 V like any other. On the STM32F103 the ADC pins are all non-FT anyway.

- **With the internal pull-up enabled**: the pull-up goes to 3.3 V, so 5 V back-feeds 3V3 through it. Simulated: with PB12 as input + pull-up, **35 µA** flows into the pin ((4.69 − 3.3)/40 kΩ). The datasheet also says not to enable pulls on an FT pin that sees 5 V.

measurements.ask: Button pressed: multimeter on the divided SIG3 (PA0) to GND
measurements.explain: 4.69 × 20k / 30k ≈ 3.13 V: above VIH (2.15 V), so it reads 1, and below 3.3 V.

measurements.ask: Same state: the FT pin (PB12) to GND
measurements.explain: The 5V pin is about 4.69 V after the USB diode and sits straight on the FT pin: with no clamp diode to 3V3, no current flows in.

measurements.ask: From your two readings, the divider ratio SIG3 / SIG5
measurements.explain: R2 / (R1 + R2) = 20 / 30 ≈ 0.667. Two thirds of a 5 V signal lands just inside 3.3 V.

measurements.ask: With a 5 V signal on an FT pin, may you also turn its internal pull-up on? (Try "input + pull-up" in the pin table.)
measurements.explain: (4.69 − 3.3) / 40 kΩ ≈ 35 µA flows into the pin. The other exception for FT pins is analog (ADC) mode: then they are not 5 V tolerant either.
choices: no: the pull-up goes to 3.3 V, so 5 V feeds back through it into 3V3 (about 35 µA)
yes: an FT pin tolerates 5 V in every mode
yes: a pull-up makes the HIGH more reliable

hints: Starting circuit: remove the wire from SIG5 to PA0 first — 5 V must never touch a pin that is not 5 V-tolerant.
Divider: SIG5 → 10 kΩ → PA0's column → 20 kΩ → GND, which shrinks 5 V to two thirds.
The FT pins are on the bottom row (PB12–PB15, PA8–PA12, PA15, PB3, PB4, PB6–PB9): wire SIG5 straight to one of them.
tests: Released: both pins read LOW (the pull-down works)
Pressed: both paths read HIGH, no current flows into the FT pin
Pressed, PA0 as ADC: below full scale
Pressed, internal pull-up on the FT pin: current flows back into the pin — no pull-ups on an FT pin with a 5 V input

tests.name: 松开：两个引脚都读到低电平（下拉起作用）
按下：两路都读到高，没有电流流进 FT 引脚
按下、PA0 设为 ADC：没有到满量程
按下、FT 引脚打开内部上拉：电流倒灌进引脚——5 V 输入的 FT 脚不要开上拉

compare: - FT 引脚：PB12 = **4.69 V**，读到 1，没有电流流进引脚。
- 松开：下拉把两路都拉到 0 V，读到 0。
- 起始电路：5 V 直接进 PA0，引脚内部到 3V3 的**保护二极管**导通。电源内阻很小，二极管电流 **52 mA**（STM32 允许的注入电流只有约 5 mA），而且这股电流把整个 3V3 电源轨“倒灌”抬高。
**为什么 FT 引脚可以**：FT 引脚上面**没有**接到 VDD 的保护二极管（换成了别的保护结构），所以输入可以到 VDD + 4 V（数据手册写 5.5 V 以内）。但有两个例外：
- **模拟模式（ADC）下不耐 5 V**——FT 引脚当 ADC 用时，5 V 照样会损坏它。STM32F103 的 ADC 引脚本来就全是非 FT 的。
- **打开内部上拉时**：上拉电阻接在 3.3 V 上，5 V 会通过它往 3V3 倒灌。仿真：PB12 设成输入 + 上拉时，有 **35 µA** 从引脚流进去（(4.69 − 3.3)/40 kΩ）。数据手册也规定 FT 引脚在 5 V 时不要使能上拉 / 下拉。

measurements.ask: 按下按键：万用表测分压后的 SIG3（PA0）对 GND
同一状态：FT 引脚（PB12）对 GND
measurements.explain: 5V 脚经 USB 二极管约 4.69 V，直接加在 FT 引脚上：它没有接到 3V3 的保护二极管，所以没有电流流进去。

measurements.ask: 用你的两个读数算分压比 SIG3 / SIG5

choices: 不行：上拉接在 3.3 V，5 V 会经它倒灌进 3V3（约 35 µA）
可以：FT 引脚什么模式都耐 5 V
可以：上拉让高电平更可靠
measurements.ask: 5 V 信号接在 FT 引脚上时，能不能顺手打开它的内部上拉？（可以在引脚表里改成“输入 + 上拉”试试）
measurements.explain: (4.69 − 3.3) / 40 kΩ ≈ 35 µA 从引脚流进去。FT 引脚的另一个例外是模拟模式（ADC）：那时它也不耐 5 V。

hints: 起始电路：先拆掉 SIG5 到 PA0 的那根线——5 V 绝不能直接碰不耐 5 V 的引脚。
分压：SIG5 → 10 kΩ → PA0 那一列 → 20 kΩ → GND，正好把 5 V 缩到三分之二。
FT 引脚在下排（PB12–PB15、PA8–PA12、PA15、PB3、PB4、PB6–PB9），把 SIG5 直接接过去。
